race_context: Richmond Community Schools (RCS) serves Richmond in Wayne County and is governed by an elected seven-member Board of School Trustees {rcs_board_page}. Its schools include Richmond High School, Dennis Middle, Test Intermediate, the Hibberd Program Building and six elementary schools, plus the Richmond Area Career Center {rcs_home}. The superintendent is Curtis Wright {wwn_academics}{wwn_arts}. A local radio report said 2025–26 enrollment fell by 21 students from the year before, with a senior class of 302 {kicks_enrollment}; this guide did not find a confirmed district-wide enrollment total.

Seats on the 2026 ballot: two at-large seats and District 3, which covers much of the city's west side {wwn_filing}{wwn_slate}. The state list shows 'vote for 1' in the at-large race, but Western Wayne News and the county election guide describe five candidates for two at-large seats {wwn_slate}{wwn_guide}{in_list}.

District 3: incumbent Kristen Brunton is the only candidate {wwn_slate}. At large: incumbents Michael Elorreaga and Kimberly Brown Pickering are running against Bruce A. Laudermilk, Tevin Roger Thomas and Roderick 'Rod' Weiss {wwn_battles}. Both at-large incumbents were appointed: Pickering in September 2023 to replace Stacy Mopps, with a term ending in December 2026 {wwn_pickering_2023}, and Elorreaga in November 2024 after at-large member Peter Zaleski resigned {wwn_elorreaga_2024}{wwn_zaleski}. Joyce Downing Mopps, an Independent, withdrew from the at-large race on July 13, 2026 {wwn_battles}.

Budget and staffing (2025–2026): in October 2025 the district projected losses from state tax changes of $584,000 in 2026, $630,500 in 2027 and $556,010 in 2028 {wwn_budget_2025}. In April 2026 an assistant superintendent projected a $2,024,436.10 shortfall in the education fund by December 2026, and the superintendent said 22 teaching positions still needed to be cut; the board asked administrators to look for savings that keep music, art and physical education {wwn_arts}. On June 29, 2026 the board voted 4–2 to approve a reduction in force of 23 positions, 19 staff and four administrative roles, which the article attributed to state legislation limiting property tax income {wwn_rif}.

Strategic and facilities plan (February 2026): the board approved a 2026–2030 strategic plan that would move the preschool center to the former Baxter Elementary, return fifth graders to elementary buildings in 2027–28 and could lead to decommissioning the Hibberd Program Building; Pickering voted no {wwn_strategic}. In January 2026 the board approved advertising for bids on Richmond High School renovation projects {wwn_sworn_in}.

Academics (2025–2026): principals reported gains on i-Ready reading and math measures at several elementary schools in June 2026 {wwn_academics}. State data show 2025 ILEARN proficiency at Starr Elementary of 18.5% in English and 30.4% in math {gps_starr}.

Forums and questionnaires: Western Wayne News published questionnaire answers from Elorreaga, Laudermilk, Pickering and Weiss; Thomas did not submit one {wwn_guide}. This guide found no 2026 candidate forum for this race.

Key differences (from the questionnaires): Weiss puts test scores and winning back students who left first and calls for a change in leadership; Laudermilk and Elorreaga emphasize transparency, spending reviews and earlier public input; Pickering emphasizes financial stability, teacher support and career pathways {wwn_qa_weiss}{wwn_qa_laudermilk}{wwn_qa_elorreaga}{wwn_qa_pickering}.

background: Former RCS teacher who teaches a course at IU East on integrating the arts in education, per Western Wayne News {wwn_arts}.
Has represented District 3 since at least 2022, when she was reelected unopposed {pal_2022_results}. She was board president in 2024 and is policy chair in 2026 {wwn_officers_2025}{wwn_sworn_in}.
path_to_ballot: Filed by petition and is listed as Nonpartisan {wwn_slate}{in_list}.

items: At the April 2026 meeting, cited declining enrollment, rising costs and the 2025 property-tax law SEA 1 as causes of the budget gap, and said doing nothing to cut costs was not an option {wwn_arts}.
Moved to approve the June 2026 reduction in force, calling the decision 'incredibly difficult' and saying it was needed so the district 'remains fiscally sound' {wwn_rif}.
Said in April 2026 she hoped for smaller cuts spread more widely, starting at the administrative level {wwn_arts}.
Voted against a staff outside-activities policy in June 2026, citing liability concerns; it passed 6–1 {wwn_academics}.

on_incumbent: Is a current board member. Said in June 2026 that the staff reductions were needed so RCS 'continues to offer excellent education' {wwn_rif}.
endorsements_finance: No endorsements or campaign finance reports were found.
gaps: Did not appear in the Western Wayne News questionnaire series for contested races; no 2026 campaign statements, website or social media were found.
Her current occupation beyond teaching an IU East course could not be confirmed.

candidates.summary: Middle school administrator and former RCS teacher and assistant principal running for an at-large seat {wwn_qa_laudermilk}.
background: Taught science at Test Intermediate School from 2004 to 2018 and was assistant principal at Dennis Middle School from 2018 to 2022; has worked in administration at Eaton Middle School since 2022 {wwn_qa_laudermilk}.
Holds bachelor's and master's degrees in education from IU East and a school leadership certification from Ball State {wwn_qa_laudermilk}.
Ran for an at-large seat in 2022 and finished fourth of 10 candidates {pal_2022_results}.
path_to_ballot: Filed by petition; the state list shows him as Nonpartisan, while Western Wayne News lists him as Independent {in_list}{wwn_guide}.

items: Lists stabilizing the district's finances among his top priorities and proposes protecting classroom resources, reviewing spending and contracts, pursuing grants and multi-year financial planning with public budget information {wwn_qa_laudermilk}.
Says course offerings and graduation pathways, including the STEAM program and applied skills courses, are working well, though access has narrowed because of state funding cuts {wwn_qa_laudermilk}.

Wants to improve trust and communication among the board, administration and community through community forums, clearer explanations of decisions and spending, surveys and listening sessions, and earlier chances for feedback {wwn_qa_laudermilk}.

on_incumbent: Says some past strengths of the district have been lost and should be restored, and that trust and communication between the board, administration and community need to change {wwn_qa_laudermilk}.
plans: Would hold forums and listening sessions and report how public input shaped decisions {wwn_qa_laudermilk}.
Says he will accept the election results {wwn_qa_laudermilk}.
endorsements_finance: No endorsements or campaign finance reports were found.
gaps: Party label differs between sources: Nonpartisan on the state list, Independent in Western Wayne News.
No website, social media or forum appearances were found.

candidates.summary: Incumbent appointed in 2023 and board president in 2025, seeking her first full term {wwn_pickering_2023}{wwn_officers_2025}.
background: Senior HRIS (human resources information systems) manager at Odyssey Consulting {wwn_qa_pickering}.
Richmond High School graduate (1997) and parent of four RCS students {wwn_pickering_2023}{wwn_arts}.
Was appointed in September 2023 to fill an at-large vacancy, with a term ending in December 2026, and served as board president in 2025 {wwn_pickering_2023}{wwn_officers_2025}.
path_to_ballot: Filed by petition and is listed as Nonpartisan {wwn_slate}{in_list}.

items: Lists stability despite state funding pressure as a top priority, and proposes both new revenue and cost cuts; points to a 2025 education foundation fund she helped set up with the Wayne County Foundation and to energy audits she requested {wwn_qa_pickering}.
Objected in February 2026 to added personnel costs in the strategic plan, such as an expanded marketing role, during financial challenges {wwn_strategic}.
Lists giving teachers the tools and support they need as a top priority {wwn_qa_pickering}.
Voted against the June 2026 reduction in force and moved to vote separately on eliminating the chief of operations position, which failed 3–2 {wwn_rif}.
Wants to expand real-world skills and post-high-school pathways and to grow the STEAM program at the Hibberd building {wwn_qa_pickering}.
At the April 2026 meeting on arts and PE staffing, said she was disappointed in the proposed solution {wwn_arts}.
Proposes listen-and-learn forums and anonymous surveys before votes that affect staff or students {wwn_qa_pickering}.

on_incumbent: Is a current board member. Voted against the 2026–2030 strategic plan, citing concerns about accountability and how the board will track progress {wwn_strategic}. Says communication among the board, teachers, staff, parents and students needs to improve {wwn_qa_pickering}.
plans: Would bring back open forums and anonymous surveys {wwn_qa_pickering}.
Says she will support any board member who is elected {wwn_qa_pickering}.
endorsements_finance: No endorsements or campaign finance reports were found.
gaps: No website or social media campaign pages were found.
Her 2023 appointment coverage listed a different employer (Air Methods); the questionnaire lists Odyssey Consulting.

candidates.summary: Incumbent appointed in November 2024 and board secretary in 2026, seeking his first full term {wwn_elorreaga_2024}{wwn_sworn_in}.
background: Works at Indiana Farm Bureau Insurance in Richmond {wwn_qa_elorreaga}{wwn_elorreaga_2024}.
Richmond High School graduate (1999) with a business degree from Earlham College and a master's from IU East {wwn_qa_elorreaga}.
Has served on Reid Health's finance committee, the Amigos board and IU East's School of Business advisory board {wwn_elorreaga_2024}.
Parent of students in the district {wwn_elorreaga_2024}.
path_to_ballot: Filed by petition and is listed as Nonpartisan {wwn_slate}{in_list}.

items: Lists fiscal responsibility and close budget oversight as a top priority; proposes a line-by-line audit of operations to cut redundancies and utility costs, public-private partnerships and sponsorships, and grants {wwn_qa_elorreaga}.
Wants updated tools and staff retention and says frontline teachers and staff are what is working well {wwn_qa_elorreaga}.
Voted against the June 2026 reduction in force and opposed eliminating the chief of operations position, saying, 'Districts our size do not eliminate that role' {wwn_rif}.
Said in April 2026 that many students find where they belong through the creative arts {wwn_arts}.
Listed early childhood education, trade and workforce pathways, aging facilities and attendance as priorities when appointed in 2024 {wwn_elorreaga_2024}.

Wants earlier, clearer communication on long-term plans, proposing a monthly digital newsletter or public advisory committee, listening sessions at libraries and parks, and short online surveys on major decisions {wwn_qa_elorreaga}.

on_incumbent: Is a current board member. Says communication about long-term planning and major policy shifts should come earlier {wwn_qa_elorreaga}.
plans: Says he will accept the certified results {wwn_qa_elorreaga}.
endorsements_finance: No endorsements or campaign finance reports were found.
gaps: No website or social media campaign pages were found.
Western Wayne News lists his middle name as 'Davis' in one article; the state list shows 'David'.

candidates.summary: Real estate business owner and longtime sports official running for an at-large seat as a Republican {wwn_qa_weiss}.
background: Self-employed for about 44 years; owns commercial and residential real estate companies {wwn_qa_weiss}.
Licensed basketball and volleyball official for 47 years {wwn_qa_weiss}.

Richmond High School graduate (1979) and parent of RCS graduates; board member and treasurer of the RHS Alumni Association, president of Circle U Food Bank and board member of Richmond Kiwanis {wwn_qa_weiss}.
path_to_ballot: Filed by petition with the Republican label {wwn_slate}{in_list}.

items: Lists raising test scores as his first priority {wwn_qa_weiss}; told the board in October 2025 that addressing low test scores should be the district's focus {wwn_budget_2025}.

Wants to raise enrollment by bringing back students who left and recruiting new ones {wwn_qa_weiss}; told the board in October 2025 he believes more than 1,000 former RCS students attend other schools and that bringing them back would ease budget problems {wwn_budget_2025}.
Says the board should keep working with legislators for changes that benefit the district {wwn_qa_weiss}.
Questioned several expenditures and priorities at an October 2025 board meeting {wwn_budget_2025}.
Would grow the PTO, keep residents informed through newspapers, radio and possibly billboards, and invites residents to contact him with questions {wwn_qa_weiss}.

on_incumbent: Says he does not see anything going well in the district now and that leadership needs to change, with the board pushing the administration to do its best {wwn_qa_weiss}.
plans: Wants to help secure the resources teachers need {wwn_qa_weiss}.
Says he will accept the outcome whether or not he wins {wwn_qa_weiss}.
endorsements_finance: No endorsements or campaign finance reports were found.
gaps: No website or social media campaign pages were found.
The figure of more than 1,000 former students attending other schools is his estimate; this guide did not find district data on it.

candidates.summary: Candidate for an at-large seat running as an Independent; no campaign statements were found {wwn_guide}.
path_to_ballot: Filed by petition with the Independent label {wwn_battles}{in_list}.
endorsements_finance: No endorsements or campaign finance reports were found.
gaps: Did not submit answers to the Western Wayne News questionnaire.
No news coverage, website, social media or forum appearances were found; his occupation and ties to the schools are unknown.
One Western Wayne News article spells his middle name 'Rodger'; the state list and the county guide show 'Roger'.
